discoveryHook.scenario: Ramon Valdez works at Logan Company assembling dolls. His hourly rate is $9. This week he worked 61.5 hours. For the first 40 hours, he earns $9/hour. Any extra hours are paid at time‑and‑a‑half ($9 × 1.5 = $13.50). His gross pay = (40 × $9) + (21.5 × $13.50) = $360 + $290.25 = $650.25. Overtime makes a big difference!

visuals.title: Abby's Differential Schedule

explanation: A [[kw:differential pay schedule]] sets different piece rates for different production levels.
The rate per unit increases as output reaches higher tiers.
Each tier applies only to the units within that range.
Gross pay is the sum of (units in tier × rate for tier) across all tiers.
This system strongly encourages high productivity.

notes: Determine how many units fall into each tier by comparing total units to the tier limits.
Units beyond the last tier are multiplied by the top rate.
formulaCard.title: Differential Pay

discoveryHook.scenario: Abby Rogers also makes dolls, but she earns different rates depending on how many she produces. The schedule: first 50 dolls → $0.50 each; next 100 → $0.62; next 50 → $0.75; over 200 → $1.25. Last week she made 300 dolls. Her gross = (50×0.50)+(100×0.62)+(50×0.75)+(100×1.25) = $25+$62+$37.50+$125 = $249.50. Higher production = higher rates.

visuals.caption: Final pay can be positive or negative depending on sales.
visuals.title: Commission with Draw Example

explanation: [[kw:Straight commission]] = a percent of the salesperson's net sales (total sales – returns).
A [[kw:draw]] is an advance paid before the commission is earned.
Final pay = Commission earned – Draw.
If commission > draw, the salesperson receives the difference; if commission < draw, they owe the difference (or it's carried over).
This method gives salespeople a regular income while still incentivizing sales.

formulaCard.title: Commission with Draw

discoveryHook.scenario: Jackie Okamoto sells dolls and earns 15% commission on her net sales. In May, her net sales were $14,500. Her commission = 0.15 × $14,500 = $2,175. However, Logan Company gave her a $2,000 draw at the beginning of the month. So her final pay for May is $2,175 – $2,000 = $175. If commission is less than the draw, she would owe the company.

formulaCard.title: Salary Plus Commission & Variable Commission
notes: For variable commission, apply each rate to the sales within that bracket.
Salary is a fixed amount per pay period.
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Gross Pay} = \text{Salary} + (\text{Total Sales} \times \text{Commission Rate})$$ $$\text{Variable Commission} = \sum (\text{Sales in Tier} \times \text{Tier Rate})$$

explanation: [[kw:Variable commission scale]]: different commission rates for different levels of sales (like differential piece rate).
Total commission = sum of (sales in each tier × rate).
[[kw:Salary plus commission]]: Gross pay = Fixed salary + (Sales × Commission rate).
These plans motivate sales growth while providing a safety net.
[[imp:Understand the tier structure before calculating total commission.]]
